tei:titleStmt.tei:title: קְדוּשְׁתָּאוֹת לְשַׁבָּת שְׁקָלִים
Qedushtaot for Shabbat Sheqalim, by Elazar ben Qallir

tei:div.tei:head: Qedushtaot for Shabbat Sheqalim, by Elazar ben Qallir

tei:lg.tei:l: Blessed are You,
o Cause, our God
and God of our ancestors.
God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob.
The Deity, great and mighty and awesome;
the almighty Deity,
who well repays kindness,
and possesses all,
and remembers the kindnesses of ancestors
and sends a redeemer to their descendants
for Their Name’s sake, in love.
Sovereign, Help
and Rescue and Shield —
Reshut
By the counsel of sages and scholars,
and the study of knowledge-understanders,
let me open my mouth in song and cheer
to thank and praise the countenance of the Dweller on High.
Magen
As of old You planned all works
By number and measure, all Yours to bring.
Given that, You told him drawn from palmed waters
Data: make census on the beautiful sandal-clad ones.
Exchanging, in revolt, the Friend’s glory for Ba’al,
What is for what isn’t, blathering in apostasy,
Zealous rage cast them out, plague overtook them
However, their comrade pled for them and balm came.
To suffer their weight and burden, he was told,
Justice to advocate for them, so as to lift the head.
Crying out: For their ransom will nations be given,
Lifting and raising them when you take the...

tei:l.tei:note: In most modern Ashkenazi practice, the catenae of verses inserted after the first three piyyutim are not recited.

tei:lg.tei:l: As is written:
And the Cause spoke to Moses, quote:
When you take the Israelites’ headcount,
personal ransom will be given for each man
to the Cause when counting them;
that no plague be among them when counting them. (Exodus 30:11–12)
And it is said:
In all its stresses They were stressed,
and Their presence’s messenger saved them;
in Their love and kindness redeemed them,
and lifted and raised them
all the days of old. (Isaiah 63:9)
And it is said:
Let Them lead peoples under us,
and nations under our feet. (Psalms 47:4)
And it is said:
Each man’s personal ransom is his wealth;
but the poor hear no rebuke. (Proverbs 13:8)
And it is said:
May he have himself a messenger,
one advocate from a thousand,
to tell a man’s justice! (Job 33:23)
And it is said:
And They will grace him and say,
“Redeem him from descending into the pit;
I have found ransom.” (Job 33:24)
And it is said:
And You, Cause, are a shield for me,
my glory and raising my head. (Psalms 3:4)
My head You have raised over every head,
And my body on the heights of town You have raised.
Love over all iniquity You have covered;
Thus, Your right hand’s shade You rose to shield me.
Blessed are You, o Cause, shield of Abraham.
You are mighty forever, Master,
You bring life to the dead, greatly saving.
You turn the wind and send down the rain.
You provide for life in kindness,
reviving the dead in great mercy,
lift the fallen,
heal the sick,
free the bound,
and keep faith with sleepers in the dust.
Who is like You, Master of Powerful Acts,
and who can be compared to You?
Sovereign, who brings death and life
and causes salvation to sprout.
And trusted are You to revive the dead —
Meḥaiyéh
Mountain-flattener, the Former and Creator of wind
Measuring and weighing the streams with wind —
No plague shall afflict those crushed of spirit;
Notifying them to give redemption for each spirit.
Scornful the scion of Seir would stand; soon,
Stood out as a snare and spine, as You saw.
Orate in assembly, You advised, tit for tat,
Organizing sheḳels from the new moon, to teach this
Portion to be read at this time,
Payment peceding the payment of the insulting foe.
Chief of seers, upon seeing the coin’s form,
Chartered the Chert to the chosen, “give a gift of this.”
As it is written:
This each who passes for the census will give:
half a sheḳel by the sanctuary-weight;
twenty gerah to a sheḳel,
half a sheḳel as an offering to the Cause. (Exodus 30:13)
And it is said:
And the sheḳel is twenty gerah;
twenty shekels,
twenty-five sheḳels,
and fifteen sheḳels
makes one maneh. (Ezekiel 45:12)
And it is said:
Better is a little to the righteous
than a whole horde to the wicked. (Psalms 37:16)
And it is said:
Evil pursues the sinners,
but the righteous are paid back in good (Proverbs 13:21)
And it is said:
For behold, the Maker of mountains and Creator of wind,
who tells humanity their speech,
making morning of night,
trampling on the high places of earth;
the Cause, God of Forces is Their name! (Amos 4:12)
Their name is combined with the people joined to Them,
And for Them they would be killed every day.
They will awake, unsheathe arm and hand upon mortals;
in pouring dewdrops to revive the dead.
Blessed are You, o Cause, who revives the dead.
Meshalesh
Quantity is set for the magnates and proletariat,
Qadis and peasants are together appraised by it.
Quarrelsome officials, should not before the assembly
Quoth: “My wealth ransoms me from my perversions.”
Replete people, that is uncountable,
Ruler along with one as young as twenty to be counted,
Regarded as punishable when warned in due process,
Rougery and iniquity to be atoned for and removed.
Shared ones in this census-share will be strengthened
Shoots, their heirs, will raise their head up to join in.
Shekels of silver, atonement, to lead their atonement,
Surely remembering the gift of all who pass.
As it is written:
All who pass for the counting
from twenty years and up
will give an offering to the Cause. (Exodus 30:14)
And it is said:
Silver of guilt and silver of sin
will not be brought to the Cause‘s house;
for the priests they are. (II Kings 12:17)
Thus, as of old, all the congregation of holy ones, in
Threefold intervals would donate holy offerings.
These were set for Temple upkeep and all fire-offerings;
The holy silver given into the priests’ hand.
As it is written:
And Joash said to the priests,
“All holy silver given to the Cause’s house,
the money of each who passes,
the money of one’s own valuation,
all the money that comes upon one’s mind
to bring to the Cause’s house.” (II Kings 12:5)
Throw glance at of our wasteful ruin, our muddy mire,
Think of our lowness and no longer let us wallow.
Then as now, proclaim liberty to free us,
That nations’ wealth may be gifted in place of our souls.
As it is written:
For I, the Cause your God,
the Holy One of Israel, am your savior;
I have given as your atonement
Egypt, Kush and Saba
in place of you. (Isaiah 43:3)
And it is said:
Since you are precious in My eyes,
you are honored, and I love you,
and will give people in place of you,
and nations in place of your souls. (Isaiah 43:4)
Those borne of Your womb, recall to lift from crushing,
Those sustained, crowned with garb of good splendor.
They mightily, strongly, ennobled You at the sea.
Thus remember the people counted as sand of the sea!
As it is written:
And the number of the children of Israel
will be like the sand of the sea,
which cannot be measured nor counted,
and instead of “You are not My people” being said of them,
of them will be said “the children of the Living God.” (Hosea 2:1)
And it is said:
I will count them more than sand;
I will end, but will still be with You. (Psalms 139:18)
And it is said:
The Cause reigns forever;
your God, Ẓíōn, from generation to generation;
praise Yah! (Psalms 146:10)
And You are holy,
enthroned on Israel’s praise. (Psalms 22:4)
El Na
Deity, please!
Who could compute all those in the count?
For they, by neither measure nor lot, can one count.
A covenant cut with them of old that their count
Never be lacking the mix from the book of the Count.
If as a pole or banner they be left down for the count,
They will not be spotted under a sixty-myriad amount.
If plague and raging pestilence brings them to account,
silver they give as atonement on their account.
And each night their souls are handed to Your account,
And each morning they are tried and held to account.
As for me, how precious to me these rules You recount!
These are the counted and the ones that count.
Keep the countings and guard those in the count,
To be like almond-flowers as they bow to Your mount!
Ḥai v-Qayyam
Living and enduring, awesome and exalted and holy!
Ere the nurseman heard When you take headcount,
He shook and quaked, “How? Consider them,
Limitless and uncountable that nation;
How could I count those ungiven to be counted?
As their root was told, ‘Look and count,’
And returned and was told ‘if you can count!’
Zillions of them, counted like the seas’ sand or the stars,
And I, how could I count them, still fruitful?”
Announced the High One to him a sign of their count,
How to compute them and stand on the account-book:
Regard the initials of their names and add up in total,
And their number’s aspect will add up in your hand.
However, their honored third was not accounted
For the royal legion its alone accounted.
Appointed from birth to be acounted for sacred service,
And their force and numbers computed from a month.
Queried he, on hearing the order Ransom given for each man,
“How can one gather up ransom?
Alas, Maker, what personal recompense could one give
And find grace before the Placer of his soul?
Looking to make this people righeous, the Holy One
showed him the form of a fiery coin in a vision.
Learning, “This will be given, they wil not delay
And for all they will say aloud what they give.”
Ineffable in strength, Yah! We cannot get You.
As You cleansed the sin of those mighty in strength,
Ruthful One, as You had mercy on Yours by the atonenent-silver,
Thus accept our lips in place of bulls!
Deity, please,
forever are You adored
and forever are You sanctified
and forever and aye will You reign and be exalted,
the Deity, sovereign, awesome, high and holy,
for You are the Sovereign,
Sovereign of sovereigns,
whose sovereignty is eternal;
tell Their awesomenesses,
recount Their strength,
glorify Their forces,
sanctify Them,
exalt Them,
cheer, song, and laudation,
mighty praises of Their glory.
Qiqlar
Till I raise my head,
as of yore,
to sanctify the Holy.
Till with just scales,
They subdue my justice;
awesome, holy!
As for what happened, these I recall,
By the upright and exalted I dwelt safe and secure.
Guilt exiled me; how can I offer my sheḳels?
Till I raise my head, as of yore, to sanctify the Holy.
Due to not weighing out my sheḳels enough
Excise to oppressors today I weigh them,
Weighting false was the sin for which I was given to the evil.
Till with just scales, They subdue my justice; awesome, holy!
Zeal I lacked in giving my coins to the Dweller;
Hence I was forced to pay drachmae to my exile’s rulers.
Tapped out are these too; I am stripped bare!
Till I raise my head, as of yore, to sanctify the Holy.
In three upright baskets of three seah each,
Collections were taken for tribute of stalled-oxen and lambs.
Lacking, since they were taken, recompense for ill-gain.
Till with just scales, They subdue my justice; awesome, holy!
Made boxes like shofars, of new and old sheḳels,
Noted donations in which they were moved,
Stolen from me, so very long ago.
Till I raise my head, as of yore, to sanctify the Holy.
Overflowing like a river, the mighty pilgrim-throng,
Flung about, and I am left like a pole on the hilltop.
Chamber of justice made waste like a ruin-hill.
Till with just scales, They subdue my justice; awesome, holy!
Quoth the bird’s nest to the most exalted hill:
Raise up, as of old, the heads of those You have borne!
Shepherds seven and princes eight You will raise over them.
Till I raise my head, as of yore, to sanctify the Holy.
Silluq
And thus, to You holiness ascends,
For You are the Holy One and Savior of Israel.
Thus You saw and numbered and ordered
and investigated and measured and computed
and weighted and gauged and gathered
and accounted and calculated and summed
and counted and enumerated and ordained
and inscribed and decreed and palmed
and apportioned and looked and understood
and comprehended and beheld and examined
and wrote and marked and traced
and encoded and indicated and engraved
and taught and made known and educated
and decreed and commanded and proclaimed
and answered and spoke and said:
Each numeration and count and sum and its numbers;
Each weight and balance and bag and its marks;
Each wet and dry volume and its capacities;
Each line and plane and measure and its limits.
How to precicely calculate every matter,
Lest a dumb calculation make all wash away.
Starting with the five-hundred-year distance
All the way down to the little finger’s breadth.
A day’s journey is ten parasangs,
And each parasang is four miles,
And the measure of a mile is seven and a half stades,
And thirty rods is the measure of the stade,
And the rod is six cubits and a span,
And each cubit is three spans,
And the span is two short-spans,
and four fingerbreadths are a handbreadth and short-span.
And just as a measure was given to measure the earth,
So too a volume was given for the generations of earth.
Starting with a hundred and sixty-six years,
All the way down to a sixth of a pinky finger.
The great sea is a third of the globe,
And is accounted as a hundred and sixty-six and more.
And its depth is twenty-four times the depth of the Reed Sea,
and the Reed Sea is seventy-two times the circuit of Giḥon,
and Giḥon is sixty times the measure of the Euphrates,
and the Euphrates is as strong as the two rivers,
and the two rivers are more than the length of the Jordan,
and the Jordan is wider than five glorious seas,
and the glorious sea is a hundred and fifty ritual-baths,
And the measure of a ritual-bath is two dry donkey-loads,
and the donkey-load is around two letekhs,
and each letekh can fit five èphah,
and each èphah makes ten omer,
and each omer is seven-quarters and a bit,
and each bit is a little under a hundredth of a səah,
and a dry səah is a third less than a wet one,
And a wet səah is a third of a băth,
and each băth holds six hín,
and a hín contains twelve lōg,
and a lōg is divided into four quarters,
and each quarter is appropriate for the four cups of salvation.
and the cup is two finger-breadth squared in area,
and its height is two-fingerbreadth minus a sixth.
And just as volume was given for the generations of earth,
So too time was given for the days of earth,
Starting with the count of six thousand years of duration
All the way down to the instants of earth.
For all existence is six thousand years,
which makes five and two-thirds cycles,
and a cycle’s count is twenty-two jubilees,
and the jubilee is seven weeks of years,
and a week of years is twenty-eight seasons,
and the days of a season are ninety-one and a third,
and a day has 576 terms,
and each term has the term’s worth of instants,
and the precise one divides the instant into arbitrary instants.
And just as a measure is given for all,
So too a weight and balance is given to all,
Starting with the talent and going to the little pruta.
The great talent is the size of two mina,
and the mina adds up to sixty sheḳel,
and the sheḳel is calculated as twenty-five sela,
and half the sela is a beqa
and a quarter is a dinar,
and the dinar is divided in half,
and a fifth of it is a ma’a, meaning five silver ma’a are in a dinar,
and the ma’a is two dupondius and an assarion,
And the assarion adds up to eight pruta.
The beqa is found to have around four hundred pruta.
These are engraved in script and expounded in speech.
And wheresoever a mortal can count,
one is permitted to measure and count.
Per one’s strength and meager posessions,
the small sheḳel-offering has been set.
And per Their knowedge is Their praise;
great is our Master, possessing much strength;
thus I hope in Them!
For Their measure and weight befits Their greatness.
All wind and snow treasuries They scaled by Their weight
and the primeval waters They measured by the handful,
and the highest heavens Their full span affixed,
and all the ancient mountains Their finger weighed,
and hills of yore upheld with Their splendid forefinger;
valley and its dust contained with Their long finger.
To pierce the dragon Their right arm is prepared.
Therein is found every measure of the universe’s make,
filling the palm of the hand is it signed;
like an amulet in a man’s hand it is sealed on Their arm
and none limit the vast searchings of Their might,
that They measured and set and arranged on high.
Beyond measure of Their throne and footstool
Is the measure of the princess, highest of all,
in length, width, depth, height, the most exalted.
For there is a limit to every ending,
but its word is forever long without end.
The universe’s measure is like a handful,
but its measure is given from arm to arm.
The universe’s measure is like the thumb to the ring-finger,
but its measure is like an endless line.
The universe’s measure is measured like a third of a cubit,
but its measure goes up past two thousand cubits.
Like the vision of the measure that the delegate saw,
a scroll twenty by ten cubits
folded, thus forty by twenty, eight hundred square cubits,
and all the universe is a third of a cubit,
So the Law is found to be wider and longer
by two thousand four hundred times than the universe,
and it was given to the universe as healing and cure,
and in its right hand long life is apportioned,
and in its left hand weighs out riches, honor, and blessing.
And it revealed all hidden secrets
and it apportioned all ennumerated measures
and it loosened all knotty issues
and it weighed and stored all storehouses
And it investigated the numerous throng of earthlings,
and gave number to the empyrean troops,
and estimated the height of the thousand celestials
which all differ in height one from another.
Some are as tall as the great sea,
and some have a height like outer space,
and some the entire universe in their stature.
And some fly through the universe in two flights,
and others fly through the universe in one flights,
and each one is hidden in their camp,
standing shushed and silent and mute in their party,
until the Sovereign of the Universe grants permission,
but they are silent until the forever people enthrones Them
and thus break out to glorify the God of the Universe.
But once they glorify they do not repeat,
for they are given again to swim in the river of fire,
from which they are hewn, new like old,
laudation, praise, and cheer to the Deity they chant.
And as the rainbow with the wing cheers,
hymn and song and strength and cheer they cheer.
And the cobra-angels, highest of all celestials,
each six-winged in their graceful forms,
over the Cloud-Rider on Their throne are set,
and to the Enthroned One in awe they perform,
seeking favor in their gracious tune.
And before every force above they answer,
and give the threefold “Holy!” to the High and Mighty,
bowing prostrate, throngs upon throngs,
to Them, glorified in the celestial troops’ throngs’ counsel,
and sanctified in thousands of myriads of earthlings....
As is written by Your prophet’s hand...

tei:note.tei:p: This brief reshut was not written by Qallir. It is inserted into the Ashkenazi rite here to justify the practice of inserting piyyutim.
A moniker for Israel. See Song of Songs 7:2.
i.e. God, based on the midrashic reading of the language in Song of Songs
Moses in this case
Referring to Haman
Literally: heart. The heart is the seat of thought in Biblical folk anatomy.
The book of Numbers, which includes a census of 603,550 Israelites.
Moses, who is said to have nursed the people Israel
Abraham, who was told to count the stars and know that his descendants would be as many as them.

The gematria of רשידנגאיזי״ב, the initials of all the tribes except for Levi, adds up to 597, which is pretty close to 600, the number of thousands of Israelites. This calculation is found in Midrash Tanḥuma Buber, Ki Tisa 5, which further explains that the missing 3,000 were those who were killed after the sin of the Golden Calf.
Levi
Cf. Hosea 14:3
i.e. that divine mercy overpowers divine justice.
Find M. Shekalim 3:2
Find M. Shekalim 6:5
Find Micah 5:4
The walking distance between earth and heaven — see B. Ḥagiga 13b
The Roman mile, a little over a kilometer. Not the imperial mile.
A stade, or stadion, is around 200 meters.
No it is not. It is around 60. Perhaps the original text read שִׁשִּׁים, an understandable scribal error.
The distance between an elbow and middle finger. Approximately 50 cm.
The distance between a pinky finger and thumb in an outstretched hand.
The distance between a pointer finger and thumb in an outstretched hand.

Seet the Midrash Konen. Translated by Gandz in “The Distribution of Land and Sea on the Earth’s Surface According to Hebrew Sources,” PAAJR, 1953, Vol. 22, pp. 32-33 — “The extent of the earth’s surface is a journey of 500 years by foot: one-third of it is desert, one-third habitable land, and one-third ocean. How much is the extent of one-third? A journey of 166 years and eight months.”
The river mentioned in Genesis 2:13, not the spring outside Jerusalem of the same name.
The two remaining rivers in Genesis — the Tigris and the Pishon.
The “cast-metal sea” in the Temple used for priestly washing, as mentioned in I Kings 7:23-26
B. Pesaḥim 109b
Also known as the kor, estimated at around 220 L.
A letekh is around 110 liters.
An ephah is aound 22 liters.
An omer is around 2.2 liters, the minimum amount obligated in taking ḥallah according to B. Eruvin 83b.
Of a qav. A qav is a bit over 1.2 liters, a sixth of a dry seah. This makes a quarter of a qav about 300 ml, or 11⁄4 cups.
A băth is around 37 liters or around ten gallons.
A hín is around 6 liters, or a gallon and a half.
A lōg is around half a liter, or two cups.
The four cups at the seder, which all must be a minimum of a quarter-lōg (B. Pesaḥim 108b)

Qallir’s “cycle” is an unclear amount. 52⁄3 of 6000 would give a cycle of 1059 years, while 22*49 would be 1078 years. Sacha Stern suggests (Calendar and Community: A History of the Jewish Calendar (2001), footnote 680) that it may refer to 1064 years, double the “great cycle” of 532 years, the amount of time between two occasions where the 19-year Metonic cycle begins on the same day of the month.
See Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:1:26. 576 is 24 squared. A term (onah) is a twenty-fourth of an hour, or two minutes and thirty seconds.
Meaning an instant is 1/576 of two minutes and thirty seconds, or 1/24 of six and a quarter seconds, or a bit over a quarter second.
As in, time is not quantized and can be divided ad infinitum.

This is a very strange opening line, because in most halakhic interpretations the talent is equal to sixty mina, not two. It has been suggested that the “great talent” mentioned here is not the normative talent, but perhaps a centenarius (B. Bekhorot 50a) instead. However, the Vilna Gaon’s followers take a different approach. See final footnote.

In this case, the sheḳel in question is the litra, which, according to B. Bekhorot 50a, is referred to as a sheḳel. This can lead to some confusion, because the litra is also elsewhere said to be equivalent to sixty sheḳel. And when discussing the sanctuary weight of the half-sheḳel offering, the weight used is is equivalent to that of the sela, and not the litra.

Thus Qallir’s original text. Followers of the Vilna Gaon emend it to כִּכָּר הַגָּדוֹל כְּגֹֽדֶל שִׁשִּׁים מָנֶה וְהַמָּנֶה מִתְחַשֵּׁב בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ סֶֽלַע — “the great talent is the size of sixty mina, and the mina is considered as twenty-five sela,” to more accurately fit the normative halakhic interpretation of the relationship between the talent and the mina.
Meaning that the beqa, approximately 7 g, as one-half the sela, is the amount of the mandated half-sheḳel offering.
Also known as the zuz, or the drachma. A sela is thus equivalent to a tetradrachm, and two zuz is one beqa, which may be one of the reasons for the specific use of “two zuz” in Ḥad Gadya.
Meaning that a ma’a, being a twentieth of a sela, is equivalent to the gerah, a twentieth of the sanctuary-weight sheḳel. The ma’a is approximately 700 mg.
A small Roman weight
A very small Roman weight
A pruta being around 20 mg
The Torah
Zechariah, who saw the flying scroll
